text:
liaison_acme: FYI ACME reported significant p99 regressions on their streaming endpoint compared to non-streaming. TTFB looks fine but total request time often 2-3x. They see first chunk then long silence before final chunk.

ops-bot: created INC-4321 for ACME escalation :rotating_light:

mike: Can you paste a minimal repro? sample request and timings.

liaison_acme: Posted the customer's test case (they're using our hosted API in us-west):
```
# streaming
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"long answer please","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

# non-streaming
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"long answer please","stream":false}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sara: I pulled up the server traces for the same request IDs. Here's a scrubbed timeline (server-side):
```
2026-03-15T10:12:01.123Z REQUEST_RECEIVED id=abc123
2026-03-15T10:12:01.210Z FIRST_FLUSH id=abc123 size=512 bytes
2026-03-15T10:12:04.890Z LAST_FLUSH id=abc123 size=8KB
```
Note the ~3.6s gap between first and last flush. non-stream path completes in 400ms for same thing.

mike: interesting — TTFB ~= 87ms (first flush) so the runtime is generating quickly but intermediate flushes are delayed. That smells like a transport/proxy coalescing issue or edge buffering.

anjali: Agree. We recently rolled a config tweak to edge coalescing window on 2026-03-14 (low-latency opt). Could be misapplied to certain routes. TAGGING @kevin to check edge rollout.

kevin: looking now. I can see a staged rollout to 40% of edge nodes, and a canary where coalesce_window_ms was increased from 10 -> 200ms for batched traffic. I need the exact route the customer hits. liaison_acme can you share the full request headers they sent?

liaison_acme: Sent headers in DM. Key bits: `Accept: text/event-stream`, `X-Client-Version: acme-web-1.2.3`, `Connection: keep-alive`.

sara: also found proxy logs for that request showing coalesce hold for 3s:
```
proxy-coalesce: id=abc123 hold_start=2026-03-15T10:12:01.215Z hold_end=2026-03-15T10:12:04.880Z reason=coalesce-window
```

anjali: That matches. So the edge is buffering after first chunk probably waiting for more data to reduce network churn. For streaming users that want low latency, that's bad.

mike: Temporary mitigations: 1) force non-streaming for the customer's route (they already use non-streaming and it's fast) 2) set a tenant override to lower coalesce_window_ms to 5ms 3) add a route rule to immediate_flush for SSE endpoints. Any of these should be quick.

kevin: I can push a tenant override (safe change) to ACME's route to set `coalesce_window_ms=5` for their tenant. Rolling now to 100% for that tenant only.

deploy-bot: deploy started: tenant-override/coalesce-window/ACME -> rollout 0% -> 100% (2026-03-15T10:20:05Z)

sara: after override we see much tighter timings for recent requests:
```
2026-03-15T10:20:12.432Z REQUEST_RECEIVED id=def456
2026-03-15T10:20:12.501Z FIRST_FLUSH id=def456 size=512 bytes
2026-03-15T10:20:12.612Z LAST_FLUSH id=def456 size=7.6KB
```
Total time dropped to ~110ms. Customer confirmed improved UX.

liaison_acme: ACME confirmed latency returned to expected levels, thanks team :tada:

anjali: Next steps: run a sweep to detect other tenants hit by the large-window rollout and either revert or add targeted tenant overrides. I'll open CH-OPS ticket to audit rollout scope.

kevin: I'll also add a guard in the edge rollout tooling to exclude streaming SSE routes by default (we shouldn't increase coalesce_window for SSE).

mike: Can we add an internal alert when p99(streaming) - p99(nonstream) > 500ms for any tenant? Quick signal.

ops-bot: created task TASK-987: add p99-streaming vs nonstream delta alert.

sara: one more note for support docs: include a short repro checklist — sample curl, look for `proxy-coalesce` logs, check route coalesce_window, tenant overrides, and temporary fallback to non-streaming. I'll push a short KB.

liaison_acme: Awesome. Passing closure to ACME. Marking INC-4321 resolved.

ops-bot: INC-4321 status -> resolved by kevin (tenant override)

mike: Great quick ops. Leaving notes for postmortem, but closure OK.

kevin: filing postmortem PR with root cause (edge rollout config included SSE routes).

anjali: thanks everyone.
